hook: Fly over Egypt at night and you will see a thin, bright ribbon of lights running north through a dark desert, then spreading into a fan near the sea. That ribbon is the Nile River. Almost all of Egypt’s people live along it. Why do people crowd into some places and leave others nearly empty?

prereq.q: A map gives one value for each state of the United States. What is the scale of analysis?
prereq.why: The data are for parts of one country, so the scale of analysis is subnational, even though the map shows the whole country.

prereq.q: People in a dry place pump water from far away and build a large city. Which idea fits?
prereq.why: Possibilism says nature sets limits but people make choices and adapt.

figure.caption: Physical factors (climate, water, landforms, soil) and human factors (jobs, transport, government, history) together shape where people live.

chain.cause: A place has water, a mild climate, flat land and good soil
chain.effect: farmers can grow enough food there
many people can live close together, and villages and towns grow

chain.cause: Towns grow on rivers and coasts
chain.effect: trade and jobs gather there, which draws even more people

chain.cause: People move to where the jobs and services are
chain.effect: the world’s people end up clustered in a few regions, with large empty areas between

ideas: Where people live is called population distribution. People are not spread evenly: most live in a few large clusters, in East Asia, South Asia and Europe.
The ecumene is the part of Earth where people live permanently. Very dry, very cold and very high places lie mostly outside it.
Physical factors (climate, water, landforms, soil) and human factors (jobs, transport, government decisions, history) work together.
The pattern depends on the scale of analysis: Egypt looks crowded on a world map, but at the local scale almost everyone lives within a few kilometers of the Nile.

misconception.wrong: Physical factors alone decide where people live, so people never live in deserts or cold places.
misconception.right: Physical factors set limits, but human factors such as jobs, government plans and technology matter too. Phoenix grew in a desert, and Brasília was built inland by a government decision.

summary: Population distribution is the pattern of where people live. Most of the world’s people live in a few clusters, in East Asia, South Asia and Europe, on low, well-watered land near coasts and rivers. Physical factors and human factors shape the pattern together, and the pattern looks different at the global, national and local scales.
